text.p: - President Milan Kucan met representatives of Slovenia's three biggest parties on Monday to discuss who should be the next prime minister. Kucan will continue talks with smaller parties on Tuesday.

- Slovenian ombudsman Ivo Bizjak said on Monday that human rights in 1996 did not improve significantly, referring mostly to slow procedures in Slovenian courts. He also warned the future government to respect human rights.
- A decision about Slovenian forces' precise role in Bosnia will be taken in next few days, a NATO spokesman said on Monday. Slovenia has offered mainly logistical support.

- Slovenian companies will participate in a new business network called "World Connection" including southeast European states. The network, based in Vienna, will start work in the next two months. One of its first tasks will be the reconstruction of Bosnia.
- Slovenian Telekom will get a 70 million marks loan from foreign banks. The loan will be used to develop the country's telecomunications by the end of 1998.

- The most likely candidates for prime minister are Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats and Marjan Podobnik of the conservative People's Party. This emerged from President Milan Kucan's talks with representatives of the biggest Slovenian parties.
- Slovenia on Monday received an unchanged DB3a credit rating for December by Dun & Bradstreet's.
